cues.text: Three shots (IMPROVE 00a). Cover, frame one, host and dialog box hidden: the job site, the question on the sign "$1,000 JOB." / "What do you quote?", chip RUN THE NUMBERS, the source line "Example math. Sources: JLC, Xero". On "costs" cut in to the bench close-up: the question on a title plate up top, the cost plank big (COST $1,000) and an empty slot after it marked "?"; Snow and the dialog box come in; the tape runs out to the $1,000 mark on "thousand". On "What" cut back out to the site: the "?" blinks on the sign.
The empty price slot on the sign blinks "?".
Room: blackboard. The tool belt behind it; the answer card rises at once and fills the screen, chip THE ANSWER: "$1,000 / 0.6" writes in big on "point six".
"= $1,666.67" lands whole under it with sparks.
"40% margin" slams in under it in the accent. The card holds big into the next take (4 s or more on screen).
Room: garage. The register. Header: THE USUAL WAY. COST $1,000 rings up; MARKUP 50% +$500 rings on "fifty".
The total rings: PRICE $1,500, display QUOTE.
Line under it: "Half is margin?" in gold.
The display splits the price into thirds, the markup third in orange, "1/3": line "$500 = 1/3 of the price".
Room: workshop. The job site. Header WHY. Row: Markup: $500 / $1,000 = 50%, "on cost" swept; the tape runs to the cost.
Row: Margin: $500 / $1,500 = 33.3%, "on price" swept; the tape runs out to the whole price.
Coins hop onto the planks; plate line: Price = what the customer pays you.
Room: blackboard. The tool belt again. Chip START FROM THE MARGIN.
The formula card: Price = Cost over 1 - margin, big, held 3 s or more.
A gold ring draws around 1 - margin; under the card the worked line "40%: $1,000 / 0.6 = $1,666.67".
Room: garage. The gauge. Dial WANT A 50% MARGIN?, the needle at a third, the gold notch at 50.
Source tag "Math: JLC" up top. Stamp DOUBLE YOUR COST; a second cost-sized block stacks on; 100% markup; the needle climbs to 50.
"= $2,000 quote" slams in.
Room: framing. The register, its display asking "?". Rule card: "$1,000 job?" then "Quote from the margin." / "Not the markup."
The rule underlined; Snow waves. Then the end card with the send line: "Send this to whoever sets your prices."
